Let \(\chi:\mathbb F_p^\times\to\mathbb C^\times\) be the quartic character with \(\chi(g)=i\), extended by \(\chi(0)=0\). Then
\[
\chi(-1)=\chi(g^{(p-1)/2})=i^{(p-1)/2}=(-1)^{(p-1)/4}=s,
\]
so
\[
\chi(-g)=si.
\]

For a diagonal quartic surface
\[
a_0X_0^4+a_1X_1^4+a_2X_2^4+a_3X_3^4=0
\]
over \(\mathbb F_p\), the primitive middle Frobenius eigenvalues are
\[
-\chi^{-\alpha_0}(a_0)\chi^{-\alpha_1}(a_1)\chi^{-\alpha_2}(a_2)\chi^{-\alpha_3}(a_3)
\,j(\chi^{\alpha_0},\chi^{\alpha_1},\chi^{\alpha_2},\chi^{\alpha_3}),
\]
where \(\alpha_i\in\{1,2,3\}\) and
\[
\alpha_0+\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3\equiv0\pmod4.
\]
There are \(21\) such quadruples. The remaining middle eigenvalue is the hyperplane class \(p\).

Here \((a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3)=(1,1,1,-g)\), so only \(\alpha_3\) contributes a coefficient. Put
\[
J=j(\chi,\chi).
\]
With the given normalization of \(a,b\),
\[
J=-a+bi.
\]
The relevant quartic Jacobi sums are:
\[
j(1,1,1,1)=-J^2,\qquad j(3,3,3,3)=-\overline J^{\,2},
\]
\[
j(2,2,2,2)=-p,\qquad j(1,1,3,3)=-p,\qquad j(1,2,2,3)=-sp.
\]

Thus the primitive eigenvalues are:

\[
-s\,iJ^2,\quad s\,i\overline J^{\,2},
\]
one eigenvalue \(-p\),
six eigenvalues \(-sp\),
six eigenvalues \(ip\),
six eigenvalues \(-ip\).

Together with the hyperplane eigenvalue \(p\), this gives
\[
P_{2,S_g}(T)
=(1-pT)(1+pT)(1+spT)^6(1+p^2T^2)^6
\left(1+4sabT+p^2T^2\right),
\]
because
\[
-s\,iJ^2+s\,i\overline J^{\,2}=-4sab.
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
P_{2,S_g}(T)
=(1-pT)(1+pT)(1+spT)^6(1+p^2T^2)^6(1+4sabT+p^2T^2)
}.
\]
